findings.issue: `stripQuoted` deletes quoted spans before detection, but shell-quoted single tokens are still real argv tokens. `findForbidden('"claude" -p --agent qa-reviewer prompt')` and `findForbidden('claude "-p" --agent qa-reviewer prompt')` both return null, while both execute as raw `claude -p --agent qa-reviewer`. This false-allows the exact recordless reviewer path N5 targets.
findings.fix: Replace the quote-stripped regex skeleton with a quote-aware argv tokenizer for provider detection. Preserve quoted single-token values (`"claude"`, `"-p"`, `"--agent"`) as real tokens, while still treating quoted multi-token blobs like `"claude -p --agent qa-reviewer"` as one non-command argument. Add fixtures for quoted command token, quoted `-p`, quoted `--agent`, and quoted literal message.

findings.issue: `roleFromAgentFlag` returns the first real `--agent` in the whole segment, not the `--agent` bound to the `claude -p` invocation. `claude -p --agent general-purpose --agent qa-reviewer prompt` is allowed by the matcher; if Claude resolves repeated options last-wins, this is another raw reviewer bypass.
findings.fix: Parse from the detected `claude` command token forward and either reject duplicate `--agent` flags in prompt mode or block if any real post-claude `--agent` value is in `REVIEW_ROLES`/`BUILD_CHAIN_ROLES`.

parsed.summary: Happy-path checks pass: the recorded `dispatch-claude.js ... --review-fallback` lane, `general-purpose`, claude-pinned judges, and research/consult roles are not false-blocked; registry derivation falls back correctly. The change still fails because current reviewer ids can evade the hard block via semantically real shell-quoted command/flag tokens.
